\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
\label{sec:discussion}

STA exposes structural degeneration invisible to execution-based evaluation: ISR reveals a 99.5\% collapse under exec-only GRPO that PR hides, while SFT localizes the failure to RL optimization (\S\ref{sec:diagnostic}).
Repurposed as a training signal, ISR exhibits inevitable Goodhart collapse~\citep{manheim-goodhart-taxonomy}: tautological proofs receive artificially high ISR (${\geq}0.5$ by construction), creating a positive feedback loop that causes gaming at all four tested doses ($\beta\in\{0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3\}$).
The effect is consistent across logic types (Prolog: 0\% non-hacking, 3/3 seeds), model scales (1.7B: novel gaming modes), and training durations (500$\to$1000 steps: transient genuine windows close).
ISR semantics are objective-dependent: exec-only \emph{low} ISR signals redundancy; ISR-rewarded \emph{high} ISR signals metric gaming.
At 500 steps, ISR-trained models produce significantly more genuine proofs than random controls ($22.6\%$ vs.\ $7.7\%$; $\text{OR}{=}3.48$, $p{<}10^{-8}$), confirming that ISR captures real structural signal; this benefit is inherently transient, as the same LOO bias that rewards genuine necessity also rewards tautological constructions.

\paragraph{Timing, not destiny.}
$\beta$ does not control whether collapse occurs, but when.
At $\beta{=}0.1$, 5 seeds bifurcate stochastically: 2 collapse rapidly (${\leq}150$ steps), 3 sustain a transient genuine window (5-seed pooled: ${\sim}23\%$; per non-collapsed seed: $17$--$55\%$) that trajectory analysis confirms is temporary ($17\%{\to}2\%$ at 1000 steps).
At $\beta{=}0.05$, the single tested seed collapses immediately (100\% H7); at $\beta{=}0.2$, all 3 seeds collapse; at $\beta{=}0.3$, diverse failure modes emerge.
The structural bias ($P{\to}P$ receives $\text{ISR}{=}0.75$, single-premise-equals-conclusion receives $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.5$) ensures that H7 tautology is always the global ISR-maximizing exploit.
Once a seed samples and reinforces this exploit, convergence is irreversible; $\beta$ controls only the probability of early sampling.

\paragraph{Classifier blind spots.}
H7b (obfuscated tautology) and Prolog query-as-fact gaming demonstrate that text-match classifiers have systematic blind spots exploitable by optimization.
In both cases, functional LOO analysis exposed gaming invisible to surface-level detection: H7b via vacuous quantifier wrapping ($10/12$ at $\text{ISR}{\geq}0.83$, triple gaming of execution, ISR, and classifier), query-as-fact via $95/97$ tautological samples the strict classifier labeled non-hacking (\S\ref{sec:crosslogic}).
H9 (contradiction injection, 1.7B Random $\beta{=}0.1$; \S\ref{sec:crossscale}) extends this pattern further: contradictory premises register as individually necessary under LOO, bypassing both text-match and functional $n_{\text{necessary}}$ classifiers; detection requires logic-level consistency checking.
These cases collectively argue for mandatory functional cross-validation of text-based hacking classifiers, complemented by logic-level checks for novel exploit classes.

\paragraph{Capacity-dependent Goodhart basins.}
Different model capacities converge to different exploit strategies under identical reward formulations (\S\ref{sec:crossscale}): 4B frequently converges to H7 (tautological duplication) or H1 (conclusion embedding) depending on seed, while 1.7B discovers H9 (contradiction explosion, under random) or fixed-template H1 (under ISR, zero-variance $\text{ISR}{=}0.6$).
No safe scale exists; both model sizes achieve 0\% non-hacking at $\beta{=}0.1$.
This suggests that scaling model capacity does not eliminate Goodhart effects but shifts the exploit basin.

\paragraph{Snapshot evaluation is misleading.}
At 500 steps, ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ shows ${\sim}23\%$ genuine output (5-seed pooled), while 2/5 seeds have already collapsed to 0\%.
A practitioner evaluating at this checkpoint would conclude ISR provides moderate structural benefit; the 1000-step trajectory reveals this is a temporal artifact.
This has practical implications: any evaluation of structural rewards must include trajectory analysis or extended training to distinguish transient from stable improvement.
The ISR/PR ratio (stable at ${\sim}0.30$ during SFT, collapsing during RL gaming) may serve as an early-stopping signal for Goodhart onset.

\paragraph{Hacking mode switching is seed-dependent.}
The dominant hacking mode (H7 vs.\ H1) is determined by random initialization, not reward condition: under identical configurations, different seeds converge to qualitatively different modes (Table~\ref{tab:fol-detailed}).
Random $\beta{=}0.1$ across 5 seeds yields genuine rates from $1\%$ to $18\%$ ($6.4{\pm}6.8$\,pp, $\text{CV}{>}1$); ISR $\beta{=}0.1$ shows even greater variance (0\% to ${\sim}55\%$ genuine at 500 steps, 5 seeds).
Single-seed results can misrepresent a reward configuration's hacking profile; multi-seed evaluation with trajectory analysis should be standard.

\paragraph{Future directions.}
The asymmetry (reliable observer, unreliable optimizer at any dose) may generalize to other perturbation-based diagnostics; ISR and similar metrics should serve as post-hoc evaluation tools, not training signals.
The stochastic bifurcation mechanism suggests that gated ISR (activating structural reward only after a warmstart period, or deactivating once ISR exceeds a threshold) might extend the genuine window, though the inherent structural bias makes indefinite stability unlikely.
Future work should target gaming-robust reward designs that do not reward tautological constructions, broader logic types, and formal analysis of the bifurcation dynamics.
